chunks: As for what Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, he said:

ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī asked him about one performing tamattuʿ hajj who did not have a sacrificial offering with him. He said: He fasts three days before the Day of al-Tarwiyah. He said: If the fasting of these days escapes him? He said: He must not fast on the Day of al-Tarwiyah nor on the Day of ʿArafah, but rather he fasts three consecutive days after the Days of al-Tashrīq.

So this does not conflict with what we presented earlier: that whoever fasts the Day of al-Tarwiyah and the Day of ʿArafah may add to them another day, because he only forbade fasting the Day of al-Tarwiyah and the Day of ʿArafah separately, and he did not forbid fasting them by way of combination, such that the addition of the third day to them is valid, as we have already presented.

key_terms.أَيَّامِ التَّشْرِيقِ: the days following ʿEid al-Aḍḥā during hajj rites
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: sacrificial offering required in the context of hajj
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, the ninth of Dhū al-Ḥijjah
key_terms.يَوْمِ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for a mutamattiʿ pilgrim who has no hady and misses the days before Yawm al-Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling for a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ hajj who does not have a sacrificial animal. It explains when the required three fasts should be observed and clarifies that if the earlier days are missed, the fasts are to be performed after the Days of al-Tashrīq, while reconciling this with earlier reports about combining the Day of al-Tarwiyah and the Day of ʿArafah with an additional day.
